description: Automation tools charge in tasks, credits, executions or runs, and the unit decides the bill. Each tool’s unit, its entry price, and one job costed.
h1: How much automation costs: credits, tasks and runs compared
answer: Most tools sell a monthly plan with a number of units: tasks, credits, executions or runs.
What one unit counts differs, so the same workflow can cost several times more in one tool than another.

root.q: What do your workflows look like?

then.answer: Any unit; compare the free tiers
then.why: For short workflows tasks, credits and runs cost about the same. A free tier may cover you.

options.label: Many steps, or loops over lists

then.q: Can someone on the team run a server?

then.why: Free to use; you pay for the server and someone's time for updates and backups.

then.answer: A tool that charges per whole run
then.why: n8n cloud and Activepieces count the whole workflow once, however many steps it has.

then.answer: Test AI credits on real inputs
then.why: AI work is priced by how much it reads and writes. Run it 10 times on real inputs and read the usage log.

body.p: Zapier does not count triggers, filters or failed steps. In Make, a step over 10 items is 10 credits.

One workflow, a trigger, a lookup and an add-row step, run 600 times a month: Zapier counts 1,200 tasks (past the 750 plan), Make about 1,800 credits (past the free 1,000), n8n 600 executions (inside Starter's 2,500), Activepieces 600 credits (inside its free 1,000).

method.h2: How to estimate what automation will cost you

steps.title: List each workflow and its runs a month
steps.body: Orders a month, emails a day times 22 working days, and so on.

steps.title: Count the billable steps per run
steps.body: Use each tool's rules from the table above.

note.text: Loops multiply: a step over 5 line items is 5 units in some tools.

steps.title: Add AI steps separately
steps.body: AI work is priced by how much it reads and writes. Run it 10 times and read the usage log.

steps.title: Add 30% for growth and retries
steps.body: Busy months and retried runs happen.

steps.title: Check what happens at the limit
steps.body: Some tools stop your workflows; some charge more. Know which before it happens.

captain.line: The best estimate is one real run. Captain tests an automation's steps on one real record before you build it, and lists every run afterwards with what it did.

wrong.title: Counting steps the wrong way
wrong.body: A five-step Zap is four tasks, because the trigger is free; a Make step over a list costs one credit per item. Read each tool's rule.

wrong.title: Polling that costs when nothing happens
wrong.body: Some tools charge for checks that find nothing. Prefer instant triggers.

wrong.title: AI steps priced like fixed steps
wrong.body: An AI step that reads long emails costs far more than one that sorts a subject line. Test with real inputs.

wrong.title: Unused credits expire
wrong.body: Make's unused credits expire at the end of the term; Lindy's monthly credits do not roll over. Buy for your usual month, not your best.

wrong.title: Quotas stop the business
wrong.body: Running out mid-month stops order logging on your busiest day. Set an alert at 80%.

faqs.q: How much does Zapier cost per task?
faqs.a: On Professional billed yearly, $19.99 buys 750 tasks, about 2.7 cents a task. Larger tiers cost less per task.

faqs.q: Is a run cheaper than a task?
faqs.a: For long workflows, yes: one run covers every step, where tasks or operations count each one. For one-step workflows they are about the same.

faqs.q: What does an AI agent cost per run?
faqs.a: It depends on how much it reads and writes. Run your AI agent on real inputs a few times and read the usage log; most builders show it per run.
